newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks inch to cautiously higher close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks inch to cautiously higher close.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended slightly higher on Monday on a mild rebound, thanks to Tokyo's own stock rebound and a central bank assurance that it would keep Taiwan's monetary policy relatively loose, brokers said.
Brokers said shrinking turnover prevented bigger gains.
The weighted index closed 29.22 points or 0.43 percent at 6,808.83. Turnover was a light T$37.2 billion.
"Despite a lack of negative news, many investors are uncertain about the market's direction and have decided to step to the sidelines," said Chen Han-chung of Yungli Securities.
Ting Kong analyst Tsao Chung-ping gave a similar assessment, saying: "Investors' worries have been eased but their confidence has not fully recovered."

Central bank vice governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Saturday that the bank had no plans to adjust its stable-to-loose monetary policy despite a recent surge in stock prices that he acknowledged was driven in part by loose liquidity.
Construction shares jumped to lead the market, up 1.41 percent. Delpha Construction rose T$1.2 or 3.96 percent to T$31.5 on active bargain-hunting.
Newcomer United World Chinese Commercial Bank, which listed last week, was up T$1.5 or 1.86 percent to T$82.
"Buying interest was scattered around lower-priced stocks which had lagged previous gains," Yungli's Chen said.
Electronics were weak, with Compal Electronics down T$1.5 or 2.38 percent to T$61.5. Computer giant Acer Inc was unchanged at T$50.
Brokers expected the market to egde slowly higher again on Tuesday, with initial resistance seen at 6,850 points.
